messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated packet loss observed from CDN POP eu-south-2 to our edge gateways — spike started ~11:02 UTC, increased p99 latency. Auto-escalation threshold crossed. Paging oncall.

Dylan (oncall): I'm on it. Marking incident P1. Any immediate customer-facing impact?

incident-bot: Symptoms: 5xx rate from eu-south-2 origin proxies up to 12% over last 10m, TCP retransmits high on ASN-level peering traces. Affected paths: eu-south-2 -> core-edge-3. Fallback routes triggered 27% of requests.

Aaron (support): Seeing a small cluster of customer reports for slow responses in EU clusters — mainly search APIs and streaming sessions. Customer tickets linked: #2345, #2346. I'll post a brief status update after we confirm scope.

Dylan (oncall): Ella, can you grab peering/device metrics and traceroutes? If it's last-mile peering, we may need to fail traffic to eu-west-3 POP.

Ella (netops): Pulling metrics now. Initial check shows spike in BGP path flaps for ASN 64521 on peering link 10G-az2. Packet loss concentrated on 10.20.45.0/24 egress queue. Running active traceroute to one affected POP.

Ella (netops): traceroute output:
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.22 (203.0.113.22), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  0.4 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  10.20.45.1  4.1 ms  4.0 ms  4.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  * * *
 5  198.51.100.1  120 ms  115 ms  117 ms (high loss)
```

Ella (netops): Looks like packet drops start at hop 3 (outside our fabric). Could be upstream ISP congestion or a bad ECN/MTU behaviour. Opening ticket with transit provider now.

Dylan (oncall): OK — while provider responds, let's reduce customer impact: 1) Enable POP failover to eu-west-3 for latency-sensitive routes, 2) adjust retry policy for streaming to tolerate transient drops, 3) increase prefix-level caching TTLs where safe. Can ops-bot push the routing change?

ops-bot: Enqueued route-failover job: job-id=rf-1843001111-1. Will start draining eu-south-2 sessions and announce backup routes to eu-west-3. ETA 2m.

Maria (eng-runtime): Can we do a partial traffic split (canary) first? Full failover risks overloading eu-west-3. Suggest 30% reroute, monitor error budget.

Dylan (oncall): Good call. Start with 30% shift. Monitor p50/p95/p99 and 5xx. If eu-west-3 holds, escalate to 60% then 100%.

ops-bot: Route split applied: 30% -> eu-west-3, 70% -> eu-south-2. Telemetry streams updated.

Rita (sre): Watching metrics now. After split: 5xx from eu-south-2 dropped to ~4%, overall 5xx decreased from 9% to 3.2%. P99 latency improved for affected customers by ~180ms on average.

Aaron (support): Posted customer note: "We're investigating increased errors and latency in parts of Europe. We're mitigating by shifting traffic to alternate POPs; some users may see brief reconnects. We'll update in 20 minutes." :thumbsup:

Ella (netops): Transit provider responded — they see microbursting on their interconnect, investigating specific fabric card. They requested we keep some traffic on eu-south-2 for correlation.

Dylan (oncall): Okay keep 30% for now. Ella, get provider's ticket number and ETA. Also request BGP community tags to steer, if available.

Ella (netops): Provider ticket #TP-99871, initial ETA to remediate 35-50 minutes. They've applied tentative mitigations (QOS tweaks) and asked us to monitor for improvements.

Maria (eng-runtime): Noting a backlog of KV-cache warms due to failover. We should expect some higher origin load to eu-west-3. Monitoring origin CPU on those nodes — currently at 42%, rising.

Rita (sre): Bringing up autoscale policy to add 2 extra instances in eu-west-3 for the next 30 minutes to absorb spike.

Rita (sre): Update: autoscale completed, origin CPU stable around 55%. No new 5xx spikes from eu-west-3.

Dylan (oncall): Good. Next: prepare a concise incident summary for postmortem. Key items to capture: timeline, provider root cause (fabric card/microbursts), mitigation steps (30% canary -> scale -> full failover if needed), customer impact (peak 12% 5xx, ~4% active customers affected in EU), and follow-ups (BGP health checks, routing playbook addendum).

Ella (netops): Provider says their hardware team will replace the suspect line card in 3 hours if QOS fixes are insufficient. They'll follow up in 45m.

Aaron (support): Updated customer note with current mitigation and ETA for next update (45m).

incident-bot: Incident P1 has been acknowledged and assigned to Dylan (oncall). Current status: mitigated (partial) — monitoring.

Dylan (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm on duty for another 35m. If this persists beyond the provider 45m update, I'll escalate to the oncall rotation lead. Rita, please take post-incident writeup. Ella, own provider follow-up. Aaron, collect customer impact numbers and affected orgs for the postmortem. Maria, attach telemetry dashboards and link replay traces.

Rita (sre): Will draft postmortem and include suggested runbook changes: add automated small-step route shift playbook, and a circuit-breaker to reduce origin load when reconnect storms detected.

Ella (netops): Provider update at +40m: microburst threshold reduced, packet loss down to baseline, path flaps cleared. Continue to monitor 20m.

Dylan (oncall): Closing active mitigation loop: shifting back to normal routing over next 10m with graceful traffic normalization. Leave follow-up tasks in incident ticket.

ops-bot: Route normalization job queued. job-id=rf-1843001111-2.

Rita (sre): Final status: Service restored to normal. Peak impact window ~ 11:02–11:50 UTC. Affected EU customers had elevated errors; support/outreach ongoing. Postmortem owner: rita (sre), due in 72h.

Dylan (oncall): Thanks team. If provider confirms hardware replacement not needed, close the provider ticket. Otherwise, follow through with scheduled maintenance. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Root cause pending provider confirmation.
